- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to revert — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates upside — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is positive and price is volatile — add 3–7% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.20 and volatility > 0.10.  
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (e.g., 10%+ below), it’s likely underestimating — adjust upward by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should start rising 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 7–10 days) — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is negative or neutral.
